title: Trade with the prevailing market trend
claim: The book frames trend identification as a core forex principle: traders should distinguish uptrends, downtrends, and sideways markets and prefer trades aligned with the prevailing direction.
support: Chapter 1 defines trend states and says identifying patterns helps traders trade with the trend.

title: Risk only disposable capital and use basic risk controls
claim: A trader should not risk more than he or she can afford to lose and should use stop-losses, limited leverage, and diversification to reduce loss severity.
support: The book explicitly ties success to risking affordable amounts and using stop-losses, multiple pairs, software, and lower leverage.

title: A trading plan must define entry, exit, and money management
claim: A forex trading plan should contain rules for entries, exits, and money management, and deviating from the plan is treated as poor trading even if a trade happens to make money.

source.section: Make Use of a Forex Trading Plan

support: Chapter 1 says a plan can be tested on historical information and then followed in live trading without discretionary deviation.

title: Major pairs are usually more liquid and cheaper to trade than exotics
claim: The book states that major currency pairs tend to have higher liquidity, narrower spreads, and lower manipulation risk than cross or exotic pairs, while exotics are less liquid and riskier.

source.section: Major Currency Pairs and Exotic Pairs

support: Chapter 2 contrasts majors with crosses and exotics in terms of liquidity, spreads, volatility, and manipulation sensitivity.

title: Bid-ask structure and quote conventions directly affect trade outcomes
claim: Forex traders need to understand base currency, quote currency, bid/ask pricing, and spread behavior because even small pricing differences compound into meaningful profits or losses at typical trade sizes.
support: The chapter explains long and short examples, quote currency mechanics, and how tiny spread differences matter in large trades.

title: Broker and platform choice are operational risk points
claim: Brokers, platforms, and account access are treated as decisive operational variables: traders should prefer regulated firms, understand fees and rollover costs, monitor account liquidity, and use demos before trusting live capital.

source.section: Brokers, Account Balance, Platforms and Tools

support: Chapter 3 warns about fraudulent brokers, emphasizes regular account checks, and discusses platform features, calculators, and support needs.

title: RSI recovery from extremes is a trend-following trigger
claim: The RSI can be used as an entry trigger by waiting for the indicator to recover from oversold or overbought extremes in the direction of the broader trend.
support: The chapter says traders enter with the trend as RSI reverses away from sub-30 or above-70 extremes.

title: Use analytical confluence instead of a single standalone signal
claim: The chapter implies that combining multiple analytical views such as moving averages, MACD, chart structure, and macro indicators gives traders a stronger basis for entry and exit decisions than relying on one indicator in isolation.
support: The text presents several technical indicators and key macro variables, then describes both technical and fundamental analysis as critical to understanding market conditions.

title: Organization and journaling support better trading decisions
claim: An organized trader should prepare before entering a trade, keep a trading plan, and maintain a journal or record of trades to create feedback for later evaluation.
support: The psychology chapter explicitly recommends organization, pre-trade thinking, and maintaining a record of trades.

title: Realistic expectations require disposable capital and emotional distance
claim: The book argues that traders should use only disposable capital, avoid trades that cause sleeplessness, and treat each trade independently instead of becoming emotionally attached to outcomes.
support: Chapter 5 connects emotional control, realistic expectations, and disposable capital to healthier trading behavior.

title: Range trading should buy support and sell resistance in sideways markets
claim: Range trading is presented as buying near support and selling near resistance when the market lacks directional trend, while positions should be exited when the range breaks.
support: The strategy section defines the range, entry timing with oscillators, and risk management by exiting if support or resistance breaks.

title: Inside-bar continuation works best on daily charts with the trend
claim: The beginner inside-bar setup is described as most effective when traded on daily charts, after consolidation, and in the direction of the prevailing trend with a favorable risk-reward profile.
support: The book explicitly says to avoid sub-daily timeframes, focus on breakout after consolidation, and trade inside bars with the trend.

title: Pin bars need trend, structure, and value context
claim: Pin bars should not be traded blindly; the book recommends using them with the trend, after structure breaks, and from areas of value because not all pin bars carry the same information.
support: The text lists specific filters to improve pin-bar odds and warns against assuming every pin bar means reversal.

title: Breakouts should wait for confirmation and predefined exits
claim: Breakout trades should use confirmation such as retests or higher volume and should define profit-taking and stop-loss exits in advance to limit false-breakout losses.
support: The breakout section discusses false breakouts, confirmation, retests, volatility, and exit planning.

title: A usable trading signal needs complete trade instructions
claim: Forex trading signals are only actionable when they specify the currency pair, timing, direction, entry price, stop-loss, and target-profit level in a clear format.
support: The chapter defines signal payload fields and later says the best signals are simple, organized, and easy to follow.

title: Automated signal services save time but can fail opaquely
claim: Automated forex signals and robots can save time and support back-testing, but they are inflexible around unusual events and can fail through crashes, technical errors, stale logic, or fraudulent performance claims.
support: The chapter praises automation for speed and back-testing, but also warns that automated accounts can break down, crash, or keep trading through bad conditions.

title: Synchronize higher- and lower-timeframe signals before entering
claim: When using multiple charts, traders should align lower-timeframe entries with higher-timeframe directional bias instead of acting on conflicting signals across timeframes.

source.section: Choosing the Right Entry and Exit Points

support: The book explicitly recommends waiting for daily timing confirmation when the weekly chart provides the core direction.

title: Stop-losses should sit beyond the market invalidation level
claim: Risk management is not just placing tight stops near entry; stop-loss orders should be placed beyond the price level that market analysis says should not trade if the setup is valid.

source.section: Placing Stop-Loss Orders at the Right Price Levels

support: The chapter warns that excessively tight stops can knock traders out before the market reverses in their favor.

title: Keep per-trade risk small and consistent
claim: The book recommends risking only a small fraction of capital on each trade, with 1% to 2% of available capital presented as a good starting point, and keeping that risk level consistent across wins and losses.
support: Chapter 8 says traders should invest small percentages per trade, gives a 1%-2% example, and warns against increasing size after a winning streak.

title: Expectancy is a practical way to test system reliability
claim: The book offers expectancy as a simple measurement for trading-system reliability by combining win rate, average win, and average loss to estimate long-run dollars earned per dollar risked.
support: The chapter works a 10-trade example and concludes that positive expectancy indicates a potentially profitable system over time.

title: Crypto chapter makes freshness-sensitive operational claims
claim: The cryptocurrency chapter claims low fees, constant access, fast transfers, and growing adoption, but it also acknowledges severe price volatility, limited understanding, and adoption friction, making the material highly freshness-sensitive.
support: The chapter mixes promotional claims about control and low fees with explicit warnings about volatility, trust, and limited acceptance.

title: Trading without knowledge or a plan is a primary beginner failure mode
claim: The book treats uninformed trading and planless trading as foundational beginner mistakes and recommends education, demo practice, written plans, and realistic goals before live deployment.

source.section: Trading Without Much Knowledge; Trading Without a Plan

support: The chapter says traders should treat trading like a business, learn first, test plans in demo accounts, and follow the plan once live.

title: Overleverage, poor money management, and overtrading destroy accounts
claim: Beginners commonly blow up by risking too much per trade, trading borrowed or needed money, overtrading unfavorable markets, and ignoring risk-reward structure.

source.section: Lack of Money Management and Overtrading

support: The chapter explicitly criticizes overleverage, oversized single-trade risk, insufficient capitalization, and trading outside favorable plan conditions.

title: Choosing the wrong broker can strand capital or degrade execution
claim: A poor broker introduces scam risk, weak regulation, bad withdrawal access, unsuitable lot sizing, poor support, and possible dealing-desk conflicts, so traders should background-check and test brokers before depositing full capital.
support: The chapter recommends checking regulation, reviews, micro-lot support, dealing-desk behavior, and demo quality before trusting a broker.

title: Passive-income promises from forex are weakly supported
claim: The final chapter markets forex signals, robots, and social trading as routes to passive income, but the text provides little evidence for durable profitability and repeatedly admits that provider research and ongoing supervision are still necessary.

source.section: How to Make Money with Forex Trading to Create Passive Income

support: The chapter uses promotional language about passive income while simultaneously warning that not all providers or robots work as claimed.

title: Signals, robots, and social trading need provenance and oversight
claim: Even when traders outsource decisions to signals, robots, or social-copy trading, they still need to verify provider quality, monitor runtime behavior, and understand that automation and copied trades can fail or be fraudulent.

source.section: Forex Signals, Forex Robots, Social Trading

support: The chapter recommends researching providers and monitoring robots while warning that many robots are frauds and trusted traders are hard to identify.
